cand.title: Club Med Punta Cana 2027 CME — French-speaking physicians
cand.excerpt: High evidence and exact competitor commitment; current accessibility is none, so value is future capture/overflow intelligence rather than open current demand.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Josh Botelho, Caméléo event-development specialist, explicitly sources hotels and event locations. Mélissa Rancourt, director of events and continuing professional development, handles scientific and logistical coordination. Both are verified commercially relevant organizer contacts, not verified signatories or confirmed individual buyers for the 2027 contract.
findings.futureEdition: Verified upcoming French-language edition within the requested horizon: resort stay February 27–March 6, 2027; actual accredited scientific activity March 1–4, 2027. The scientific title is “Mise à jour multi-spécialités : chirurgie, microbiologie et infectiologie, médecine interne et ORL.” These are activity/stay dates, not publication dates. Do not merge the separate English-language week of March 6–13 into this candidate.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel profile and the published family-oriented all-inclusive CME format: Wyndham Alltra Punta Cana is a plausible guestroom-led resort alternative for a future edition, not a city-convention play. Its supplied approximately 300-person conference capacity is only a ceiling to test, not evidence that this group fits. Attendance, room mix, audiovisual needs, French-language support and breakout requirements must be obtained before qualification. No current room-night estimate is defensible.
findings.venueCommitments: Club Med Punta Cana is the publicly announced event host and accommodation destination for the February 27–March 6, 2027 French-language package. The edition page advertises “DERNIÈRES CHAMBRES”; the programme requires accommodation through Caméléo DPC. This establishes an edition-specific marketed venue/lodging commitment, not merely a preferred-hotel listing. No signed contract, room-block quantity, allocation, exclusivity, attrition or release date is published in the reviewed materials.
findings.historicalRotation: The official archive records Club Med Punta Cana scientific events in 2016, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; multiple 2022 entries should not be treated as a single identifiable French-language edition. Edition-specific programmes verify March 4–7, 2024; March 3–6, 2025; March 2–5, 2026; and March 1–4, 2027 at the same host. Repeated Punta Cana hosting is verified; destination rotation of this particular spring-break series is not. Other destinations, including Michès and Cancún, occur in the wider organizer portfolio and are not proven replacements for this edition.
findings.accommodationSourcing: The 2027 French programme explicitly states that accommodation must be booked through Caméléo DPC. Booking enquiries go through the event form, info@cameleomed.com or 1-800-590-5995. Participant sales are advertised, but hotel procurement is not advertised as open. Treat this edition as committed elsewhere; neither a public hotel RFP nor an external overflow accommodation arrangement was identified. No local DMC or separate procurement platform is named.
findings.organizationStructure: Cléo describes itself as a nonprofit continuing-professional-development organization supervising scientific committees and programmes. It is the named presenter of this edition. Caméléo is the event/travel delivery and compulsory accommodation-booking pathway; its FAQ identifies a Québec-licensed travel agency, permit 703160. This is a nonprofit scientific presenter plus commercial event/travel intermediary, with Club Med as host resort—not three interchangeable owners. Legal ownership links, precise contracting entity and any destination subcontractor remain unverified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Club Med Punta Cana is the edition-specific incumbent. Consecutive verified hosting and Caméléo’s separately published long-standing Club Med collaboration create a relationship barrier (commercial inference), not proof of an exclusive agreement. “Last rooms” is qualitative inventory pressure only: it does not quantify the block, establish resort-wide sellout or prove overflow demand. No Wyndham allocation or off-site attendance permissions were found.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Josh Botelho through the official Caméléo channel and copy/request Mélissa Rancourt. Acknowledge Club Med’s 2027 commitment; seek a future-cycle supplier introduction, not a displacement quote. Ask when the next Punta Cana hotel review opens, whether non-Club Med resorts may compete, who contracts lodging/meeting space, and for historical pickup, peak rooms, family mix and plenary/breakout needs. Offer a targeted Wyndham site inspection and preliminary fit brief only after interest. Ask whether the advertised last-room position requires organizer-approved overflow; do not offer or forecast overflow as established business.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: No evidenced open hotel-sourcing opportunity for Wyndham for this confirmed 2027 edition. The published venue and compulsory Caméléo booking route make replacement capture commercially inaccessible on current evidence; this is a sales assessment, not proof that amendment or overflow is contractually impossible. Participant booking availability must not be presented as supplier accessibility.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship-development / recurring competitive-capture prospect, not qualified open demand. Recurrence is evidenced through consecutive 2024–2027 programmes, but no 2028 edition, date, venue or sourcing window was found in the reviewed upcoming calendar/programmes. Do not assign an inferred 2028 spring-break date. Future capture depends on willingness to consider a non-Club Med host and fit with the actual room and meeting brief.
